AMERICA MAGAZINE: "Is the World Cup distracting Mexico from news of crimes and disappearance?"
July 2, 2026 | 🟡

📰 The Jesuit review asks if Mexico's World Cup is burying the missing-persons crisis. Its sharpest point isn't the football — it's that authorities opened an investigation into the madres buscadoras' protest, not the disappearances behind it. 🇲🇽

• "I have to disguise myself as a duck, so the president looks at us." — protester's sign, madres buscadoras
• Government "tries to portray a reality that doesn't exist, claiming there's been progress on security." — activist Jorge Verástegui González

CBS SF / NEWSWEEK: California venues cancel World Cup watch parties after violence
July 4, 2026 | 💀

📰 Shootings and stabbings tore through Bay Area watch parties — one man killed in San Jose, two shot in San Francisco — so California venues canceled their screenings. US outlets filed it under "Mexico fan violence." The venues, and the guns, are American. 🇲🇽

Meanwhile the UK issued a World Cup travel warning about Mexico's "crime and violence."

• Newsweek: "Mexico-England Match Prompts Security Crackdown After Fan Violence"
• San Jose scrapped its San Pedro Square screening entirely.

CHARLOTTE OBSERVER: "Drug cartel used North Carolina home as stash site for gun smuggling"
July 5, 2026 | 💀

📰 ATF seized 140 firearms — including two .50-caliber rifles — in Lincoln County, NC, staged to be smuggled south to the Sinaloa cartel. The headline blames the "cartel." The guns were bought in America. 🇲🇽

Roughly 70% of guns traced from Mexican crime scenes come from US dealers. The "iron river" runs one direction, and it isn't north.

• "This investigation pulls the plug on an extremely dangerous firearms trafficking operation." — ATF's Alicia Jones
• 140 guns, two .50-cal rifles, one North Carolina house.

🇲🇽🌎 PLAN MICHOACÁN: 300 MILLION PESOS INTO TOURISM, NOT JUST ARRESTS

Fonatur director Sebastián Ramírez announced a historic 300-million-peso investment to rebuild tourism in Michoacán under the Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice — the economic half of a strategy that has already cut the state's homicides by 46%.

🚨🇲🇽 THE NUMBER THAT WORRIES THE OECD: 6% OF GDP NOW GOES TO MEXICO'S ELDERS

Welfare pension spending rose 6.3% in the first five months of 2026 — 693 billion pesos in contributory pensions alone — as universal pensions for older adults climbed from 3.4% of GDP in 2018 to nearly 6% today, per SHCP. What the OECD flags as a "sustainability risk" is the largest sustained transfer to the elderly in Mexican history.

🚨🇲🇽 STATE OF MEXICO CHOKES OFF EXTORTION — 30.6 MILLION PESOS PROTECTED

Governor Delfina Gómez's security strategy in the State of Mexico has blocked more than 30.6 million pesos in extortion losses to businesses and families, targeting the collection networks directly instead of leaving communities to pay the "cuota."

🇲🇽🌎 217 ASSEMBLIES IN ONE WEEKEND: "DEFEND OUR NATION FROM FOREIGN INTERFERENCE"

Morena's national leadership is holding 217 public assemblies across the country this weekend, part of Sheinbaum's sovereignty campaign, with a stated purpose: to "defend our nation from foreign interference and disinformation."

🇲🇽🌎 US EPA ADMITS IT — MEXICO KEPT ITS WORD ON THE TIJUANA RIVER

Washington's own Environmental Protection Agency publicly recognized that Mexico is meeting the commitments it made under the 2025 binational accords to clean up the Tijuana River, praising the progress "achieved by both countries." Mexico has already completed five sanitation projects — including the San Antonio de los Buenos treatment plant — while pouring 1.7 billion pesos into the Arturo Herrera and Morita plants.

🇲🇽📱 SHEINBAUM ASKS THE QUESTION BIG TECH DOESN'T WANT ASKED: "WHO CONTROLS AI?"

Mexico will open a national debate on regulating social media and artificial intelligence once the World Cup ends — and Sheinbaum framed it as a question of power, not censorship: "Who controls AI? How many companies own the platforms, and how is that power concentrated?" The stated aim: shield children from algorithmic addiction and set democratic rules for the tech giants that answer to no government.

🚨🇲🇽 WASHINGTON SPENT $820 MILLION "FIGHTING DRUGS" IN MEXICO — THE REAL PRODUCT WAS INFLUENCE

A Contralínea investigation details how the US State Department's INL bureau poured $819.8 million into Mexico from 2019 to 2024 under the "war on drugs" banner — money that flowed to NGOs, "anti-corruption" labs and consultants shaping Mexican security and justice policy from the inside. One advisor to a US-funded lab, Roberto Patiño, had backed Guaidó's failed coup in Venezuela. As sovereignty came back, the money dried up: from $232 million a year under early AMLO to $47.6 million in Sheinbaum's first year.
